react_result.final_narrative_text: The treatment group exhibits a pronounced perturbation of the arachidonic acid cascade. Cross-paradigm analysis reveals Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the dominant pathway, confirmed by three independent methods: RaMP multi-database ORA (FDR = 1.39×10⁻¹², fold-enrichment = 1251), Mummichog m/z-direct activity (p = 0.0079, 11/11 network compounds overlapping), and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (KEGG:hsa00590 as top hit). Five input metabolites map to this pathway: arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219), leukotriene A4 (KEGG:C00909), 5-HETE (KEGG:C04805), 15-HETE (KEGG:C04742), and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2 (KEGG:C14717). The 5-lipoxygenase products (5-HETE and LTA4) and the cyclooxygenase-derived 15-deoxy-PGJ2 are simultaneously elevated, indicating coordinated activation of both the LOX and COX branches of the eicosanoid pathway. Glycerophospholipid metabolism emerged as a secondary Mummichog hit (rank 2, p = 0.0205), consistent with arachidonic acid release from membrane phospholipids. The remaining three metabolites (dehydroascorbic acid, methylmalonic acid, L-serine, 6-methylmercaptopurine) are functionally peripheral to the lipid-centered signal but do not form a coherent secondary module at significance threshold. The biological story is one of targeted eicosanoid network dysregulation, with arachidonic acid serving as the central hub and 5-HETE / 15-HETE as the primary functional effectors.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on the same biological module: the arachidonic acid eicosanoid cascade. RaMP multi-database ORA identifies Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the top-ranked hit with FDR = 1.39 × 10⁻¹², fold-enrichment = 1251, and 5 of 9 input metabolites (5-HETE, 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2, 15-HETE, arachidonic acid, and leukotriene A4) mapped to the 27-member pathway roster. Mummichog m/z-direct activity independently recovers the same metabolic domain as its top hit — Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism, p = 0.0105) with 11/11 network compounds overlapping — confirming that the signal is not an annotation artefact. Glycerophospholipid metabolism (MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism, p = 0.0229) ranks second in Mummichog, consistent with the known route of arachidonic acid liberation from membrane phospholipids prior to enzymatic oxidation. The four remaining metabolites — dehydroascorbic acid, methylmalonic acid, L-serine, and 6-methylmercaptopurine — do not appear in the top hit pathway under the current annotation threshold. Arachidonic acid is the central substrate; 5-HETE, 15-HETE, leukotriene A4, and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 are downstream products representing both 5-lipoxygenase and cyclooxygenase branch activity.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The treatment group exhibits a pronounced perturbation of the arachidonic acid cascade. Cross-paradigm analysis reveals Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the dominant pathway, confirmed by three independent methods: RaMP multi-database ORA (FDR = 1.39×10⁻¹², fold-enrichment = 1251), Mummichog m/z-direct activity (p = 0.0079, 11/11 network compounds overlapping), and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (KEGG:hsa00590 as top hit). Five input metabolites map to this pathway: arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219), leukotriene A4 (KEGG:C00909), 5-HETE (KEGG:C04805), 15-HETE (KEGG:C04742), and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2 (KEGG:C14717). The 5-lipoxygenase products (5-HETE and LTA4) and the cyclooxygenase-derived 15-deoxy-PGJ2 are simultaneously elevated, indicating coordinated activation of both the LOX and COX branches of the eicosanoid pathway. Glycerophospholipid metabolism emerged as a secondary Mummichog hit (rank 2, p = 0.0205), consistent with arachidonic acid release from membrane phospholipids. The remaining three metabolites (dehydroascorbic acid, methylmalonic acid, L-serine, 6-methylmercaptopurine) are functionally peripheral to the lipid-centered signal but do not form a coherent secondary module at significance threshold. The biological story is one of targeted eicosanoid network dysregulation, with arachidonic acid serving as the central hub and 5-HETE / 15-HETE as the primary functional effectors.
